title: Channel Experiments
description: Bullseye channel-experiment records (`bets/<bet-id>/channels.json` in the portfolio repo, written by scripts/channel.py — chief-wiggum#241). Records range over the FIXED 19-channel enum (Weinberg & Mares, *Traction* 2014); `brainstorm` seeds all 19 so unfashionable channels are considered, ranking is human. Per-channel state machine: brainstormed → ranked → testing (≤3 concurrent) → focused | rejected, with focused → testing re-entry on saturation (journaled, reasoned). Gates (report-only by default per docs/gate-rollout.md): experiment completeness — a record claiming results without a measured CAC AND customers_acquired is invalid, and a referral experiment without a recorded baseline_input_flow is invalid the same way (referral is a multiplier on an existing acquisition stream, not a source — Balfour); exactly-one-focused-channel; measured channel-CAC ≤ the bet's declared target_cac_usd (skipped when absent); sales-led channels flagged while headcount 0.

channel.description: The fixed 19 traction channels (Weinberg & Mares). Closed enum on purpose: brainstorming must cover all of them. `sales` and `business-development` are sales-led (flagged while headcount 0); `viral-marketing` is the referral/WOM channel (baseline_input_flow required with results); `search-engine-marketing`, `social-and-display-ads`, `offline-ads` are paid channels behind the paid-spend unlock gate (pmf_score ≥ 40%, n ≥ 40 — docs/business-factory.md §4); AI distribution surfaces (GPT store etc.) count under `existing-platforms`.

status.description: Bullseye state. ≤3 concurrent `testing`; exactly one `focused` per bet. Maintained by scripts/channel.py only — every transition is journaled into the portfolio hash chain.

rank.description: Human-assigned Bullseye rank (1 = most promising). Ranking is a human act; the CLI records it.

hypothesis.description: What this channel test is expected to show, falsifiably.

budget_usd.description: Cheap-test budget. Actual spend goes through the bet ledger and counts against the envelope like any other spend.

customers_acquired.description: Customers attributable to this channel test. Required (with a measured CAC) once the record claims results — a test without it is invalid.

measured_cac.description: Measured acquisition cost per customer for this channel. Required once the record claims results. For the referral channel, referral_metrics.reward_cost_per_attributed_signup is accepted in its place.

icp_quality_note.description: Who actually showed up — ICP fit of the acquired customers, not just their count.

verdict.description: Short human verdict. An underwater channel's verdict must say so (measured CAC above the bet's target/LTV floor), not let spend drift.

baseline_input_flow.description: Referral/WOM only: the existing acquisition stream the loop amplified (Balfour: sustained K > 1 is rare — referral is a multiplier, not a source). A referral experiment with no recorded baseline flow is invalid, same as a test without measured CAC.

referral_metrics.description: Declared metrics of the stamped `referral-invite-loop` pattern (#139), read as this experiment's measured values — a validation rule on the record, not a platform integration.

reward_cost_per_attributed_signup.description: The pattern's CAC figure — accepted as the referral experiment's measured CAC.

history.description: Per-record transition trail (the authoritative journal is the portfolio hash chain).
